provenance.status: RECONSTRUCTED FROM THE COMMITTED REPORT -- NOT THE ORIGINAL GENERATION RECORD
provenance.why: Phase 3's candidate generation, its adversarial verification and its completeness audit were carried out in a Claude Code session whose transcript was never exported (`Claude Conversation 3 (kinda).txt` records the failed export). Every other Phase-3 claim traces to a script, a JSON and a log; this one existed only as report prose. This file closes that gap as far as it can be closed, and says plainly where it cannot.
provenance.what_is_recovered: The final candidate set, verbatim from the report's own tables: the 14 ranked rows of §6.3 with every column, the refuted candidate and its reason, the three candidates referred to Elliot and their reasons, and the two merged pairs with the algebra given for each.
what_is_NOT_recovered: The pre-merge proposal text for the four candidates that became two. §6.1 states the merge conclusions and their algebra, but the original wordings are gone, so the merge claims cannot be re-checked against what was actually proposed.

Which eight of the eighteen were added by the completeness audit. §5 names two of them (#2 current normalisation and #4 readout capacity); the other six are not attributable from the committed record and are recorded as null rather than guessed.

The mapping of each candidate onto the six Phase-1 areas. §9 says the set spans them; it does not say which candidate sits where. `family_reconstructed` below is this file's inference from the candidate text, is labelled as such, and is not evidence.
What the adversarial verification consisted of, beyond the three criteria §6 names (the §4.6 ruling, jiterator's elementwise-only and 8-input limits, and the corrected cost constants).
provenance.rule: No field in this file may assert something the committed record does not support. Where the record is silent the value is null and the reason is stated.

counts.note: The report's §6 and §9 give these as a list of counts rather than an arithmetic chain, and the chain only closes one way: the 18 is the final set, and the two merges reduced 20 proposals to it. Report rev 2 restates §6 and §9 to match this file.

merges.basis: Algebraically identical, not merely similar. Expanding the slow compartment, w*vs_t = w*beta_s*vs_{t-1} + w*cur_t, so one is the other with g = w*beta_s plus a scalar rescaling of the current that the layer's own Linear absorbs. Both compile to EXP_002's N2 with the same kernel signature.

candidates.name: Re-measure σ on a two-state neuron
candidates.note: σ was measured at *one* configuration; every verdict assumes it transfers
candidates.status_after_exp_004: PROMOTED TO BLOCKING by EXP_004's decision cell (§4, §10.10): every further 2σ verdict in this family rests on a sigma measured on a one-state neuron. EXP_004 §10.7 gives a weak n=3 reading (0.00487 carried against 0.00461) that does not close it.

exp_005.result: sigma does NOT transfer: carried sd 0.00313 at n=7 against the baseline's 0.00461 (0.680x), fresh 0.658x. The two-compartment family's bar is 2 sigma = 0.00627. The failure is in the safe direction -- the inherited 0.00922 was conservative -- so no adopted verdict moves; EXP_004's adoption strengthens from 29.2 to 42.9 sigma.
exp_005.qualification: n=7 cannot demonstrate the difference: the variance ratio is 0.462 and an F(6,4) test only resolves ratios outside [0.1605, 9.20]. The band was failed; the difference was not established.
consequences: sigma is not a project constant -- #14 is closed for THIS neuron, not in general. Any future structurally-different arm needs its own sigma.

The §6.2 per-context bars are arm-specific in SHAPE, not only scale (EXP_005 §9.5): the baseline's excess-sd collapses beyond its 7-character horizon while this arm's persists to c=127, 21x larger at c=16. The criterion must be calibrated per arm, which is more expensive than Phase 3 priced it.
The per-context bar is built on the wrong scale (45x too small at c=127), but the count does not move: 5 of 128 at c=3..7 under all three bars. The fix is REFERRED to Elliot, not applied.
